requirements.title: Logical intrinsic operations express logical computations and produce logical results
requirements.definition: A logical intrinsic operation expresses a logical computation and, when evaluated, produces a result of type logical. The permitted operand types are not redefined here; they are the logical operand rules specified in 10.1.5.1.

pending.operand-type-delegation: PENDING  source-use plan records that permitted logical operand types are owned by S10.1.5.1-005. Any nonlogical operand diagnostic/control belongs there unless this subclause's interpretation is the only failing property.

requirements.oracle:
Use only literal logical values or standard logical inquiries. Truth-table controls must not contain operand side effects, function-call counters, undefined branches, or any assertion that .AND. or .OR. skipped an operand; Fortran does not require short-circuit evaluation. Grouping of an associative intrinsic logical operation is not value-observable, so any future grouping witness must be a valid non-associative defined extension attributed to 10.1.6 and 15.4.3.4.2.

The result-type witnesses pass (.TRUE. .EQV. .FALSE.) and (.NOT. .FALSE.) directly to LOGICAL dummy arguments whose bodies check the hand-derived truth values. No result is first assigned to a declared LOGICAL variable whose declaration would launder the expression type.
